items.label: f04-footer-limits
items.front: What does the count footer in oms.snapshot.txt detect, and what does it not?
items.back: A mismatch detects ordinary truncation or missing records. It is not a checksum and does not resist intentional edits that also change the counts.

items.label: f02-transition-graph
items.front: Give the order status transition graph.
items.back: DRAFT to SUBMITTED or CANCELLED; SUBMITTED to PAID or CANCELLED; PAID to SHIPPED or CANCELLED. SHIPPED and CANCELLED are terminal. Cancelling from PAID is a local status change only; there is no refund integration.

items.label: f03-what-is-still-missing
items.front: The aggregate, the snapshot validation and the atomic file save each protect something. What do none of them provide?
items.back: Authenticated ownership, concurrent request handling, cross-process stale-write detection, and payment idempotency. Those are the next lessons when the CLI becomes a web application.

items.label: f01-derived-totals
items.front: How are subtotal and total computed in the delivered Order, and why?
items.back: getSubtotal sums the current line totals and getTotal subtracts the discount. Deriving them leaves fewer facts to keep in sync; each OrderItem still keeps its own line total, maintained by its quantity method.

items.prompt: An order has 3 units at 10.00 and a discount of 25.00. Menu 14 asks to change the quantity to 2. What happens?

choices.text: Accepted, with the discount lowered to 20.00 and a total of 0.00
Accepted, with the discount cleared and a total of 20.00
Accepted, with quantity 2 and a total of -5.00 until the next save
Refused, so quantity stays 3, discount 25.00 and total 5.00

choices: Accepted, with the discount lowered to 20.00 and a total of 0.00
Accepted, with the discount cleared and a total of 20.00
Accepted, with quantity 2 and a total of -5.00 until the next save
Refused, so quantity stays 3, discount 25.00 and total 5.00

items.explanation: setItemQuantity builds a candidate line and checks the proposed subtotal (20.00) against the discount before replacing anything; validateSubtotal throws "Reduce the discount before reducing the subtotal." Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: A caller reads an order with service.findById, then calls getItems().get(0).setQuantity(99) on the result. What changes?

choices.text: Nothing stored, as the order and its items were both handed out as copies
Nothing, because setQuantity throws on an item that was read from a list
The stored line quantity only, while the cached total stays the same
The stored order, whose total grows because the item object is shared

choices: Nothing stored, as the order and its items were both handed out as copies
Nothing, because setQuantity throws on an item that was read from a list
The stored line quantity only, while the cached total stays the same
The stored order, whose total grows because the item object is shared

items.explanation: findById returns order.copy(), and getItems maps every line through OrderItem.copy. setQuantity succeeds on that copy only. Verified in a probe (stored total still 15.00).

items.prompt: A brand-new DRAFT order has no items. In menu 11 the user chooses SUBMITTED. What does the app print?

choices.text: Could not update order status: An empty order cannot be moved to SUBMITTED.
Order status updated.
Could not update order status: Invalid status transition from DRAFT to SUBMITTED.
Could not update order status: An empty order cannot enter that status.

choices: Could not update order status: An empty order cannot be moved to SUBMITTED.
Order status updated.
Could not update order status: Invalid status transition from DRAFT to SUBMITTED.
Could not update order status: An empty order cannot enter that status.

items.explanation: The service check for empty orders names only PAID and SHIPPED, so it passes; Order.setStatus then applies requiresItems, which includes SUBMITTED, and throws its own message. Verified in a probe.

items.prompt: A SUBMITTED order has exactly one line and no discount. The user removes that line with menu 7. What happens?

choices.text: Refused, since a submitted order must keep at least one item
Refused, since SUBMITTED orders cannot be edited at all
The line is removed and the order goes back to the DRAFT status
The line is removed, leaving an empty SUBMITTED order

choices: Refused, since a submitted order must keep at least one item
Refused, since SUBMITTED orders cannot be edited at all
The line is removed and the order goes back to the DRAFT status
The line is removed, leaving an empty SUBMITTED order

items.explanation: removeItemByProductId checks status == SUBMITTED && items.size() == 1 and throws "A submitted order must keep at least one item." SUBMITTED is still editable for other changes; a DRAFT order may lose its last line.

choices.text: One notebook line of 1 unit, as adding a product again replaces its line
Two notebook lines, 3 units and 1 unit, each with its own price snapshot
Nothing new, as a product that is already on the order is refused
One notebook line of 4 units, still at its own 10.00 price snapshot

Two notebook lines, 3 units and 1 unit, each with its own price snapshot
Nothing new, as a product that is already on the order is refused
One notebook line of 4 units, still at its own 10.00 price snapshot

items.explanation: addOrMergeItem finds the existing productId and calls increaseQuantity on that line, keeping its captured name and unit price. Verified in a probe (1 line, qty 4, unit 10.00).

items.explanation: readMoney passes the parsed value to DomainValues.money, whose setScale(2, UNNECESSARY) throws; readMoney catches it, prints its own hint and returns null, so the flow stops. Verified with piped input.

choices.text: Starts with empty data and overwrites the snapshot on the next save
It prints the reason, then calls System.exit(1) so scripts see a failure

choices.text: Subtotal 20.00, discount 5.00, total 20.00, as totals are cached on save
Nothing: startup stops, as a saved discount fails the empty-order check
Subtotal 20.00, discount 0.00, total 20.00, as reload clamps the discount
Subtotal 20.00, discount 5.00, total 15.00, all as they were before

Nothing: startup stops, as a saved discount fails the empty-order check
Subtotal 20.00, discount 0.00, total 20.00, as reload clamps the discount
Subtotal 20.00, discount 5.00, total 15.00, all as they were before

items.explanation: parseRows groups all item rows by order and calls Order.restore with the complete list, so the discount is checked against the full 20.00 subtotal. The regression test reloads 5.00 and 15.00. (The original app reset it to 0.)

items.prompt: Why does FileDataStore rebuild orders with Order.restore instead of creating a DRAFT and replaying addOrMergeItem and setStatus?

choices.text: Replaying would be correct but slow, as each call recalculates every total
addOrMergeItem cannot add lines whose product is not in the catalog yet
Replay hits the PAID edit block and moves updatedAt; restore avoids both
restore skips validation entirely, so damaged files can still be repaired

choices: Replaying would be correct but slow, as each call recalculates every total
addOrMergeItem cannot add lines whose product is not in the catalog yet
Replay hits the PAID edit block and moves updatedAt; restore avoids both
restore skips validation entirely, so damaged files can still be repaired

items.explanation: A paid order loaded from disk must regain its items and discount without being reopened for editing or getting a new update time. restore builds the complete aggregate and validates it directly.
